content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification:** deviation (fails fallback; walk-away territory).

**Why:** The three-year Agreement (§ 8.1) gives us no convenience exit at all — § 9 covers only material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2) and security/SLA/law/IP failures (9.3) — and § 2.1 affirmatively strips "reduction or termination rights" from the USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment. Non-renewal notice (§ 8.2) and the force-majeure exit (§ 27.3) are conditional, not convenience rights. Vendor has no convenience right today, which we preserve and lock in.

**Cure (preferred level, two surgical ops):**
1. New § 9.4 — Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, on 30 days' written notice; Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term.
2. § 2.1 — replaced the trailing "without reduction or termination rights" with "subject to Customer's termination rights under this Agreement" so the take-or-pay clause no longer contradicts the new right.

The pro-rata refund element is already met by § 10.2 ("Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination"), so no refund language was added.
